issues.title: Redesign the launcher UI
issues.pin: This panel is the target. Today the same controls are one flat column with no grouping and no first step.

issues.title: Shared lobby URL with port claiming
issues.pin: The room code is the lobby, top right, and clicking it copies the link. Two players pair for real, and a phone-shaped browser is one of them: measured over the routable tailnet address, both claim a port and the touch overlay draws. Two defects had to go first, and both hid behind loopback. signal.mjs sent claims as an object while lobby.mjs calls .indexOf on it, so every state event threw and no claim ever rendered (9fee67ca). Then crypto.randomUUID, which exists only in a secure context: http://127.0.0.1 is one by exemption and a tailnet IP is not, so the page could mint neither a room nor an identity on the only origin a visitor uses (f303d4a8). A third defect was in the offer itself: gathered() cut ICE gathering off after 3 seconds without checking that a srflx candidate had arrived, so on a slow network the offer went out with LAN addresses only. Measured here the first srflx lands at 11 ms while gathering is still open after 12 s, so the cutoff is now a ceiling and the srflx arrival releases the offer (c51bf783). Also measured over an https origin, which is what a shared link really has and which plain http on an IP is not: both ports claim and the data channel opens there too. On the two-seat path this is done: two players pair over a real shared link and both claim a port. Ports 3 and 4 are no longer counted here -- they are not a transport gap but an engine one (#40, out of goal), and the lobby now says so on the tile instead of promising a fix: an unreachable tile reads "2P only" (lobby.mjs:347) and the spec's P3/P4 are drawn unavailable to match. The link is a private tailnet address, shared privately rather than published, so the server needs no auth gate of its own. Requested and not yet drawn on the board: drop the "copy link" text from the room-code button (comment 3076), and add a list of all open lobbies to join (comment 3101).

issues.title: Lobby replaces the mode list
issues.pin: One persistent room per URL, shipped in 00480d1b: lobby.mjs mints the room with replaceState and draws four port tiles, 42 tests cover it. The mode links are gone, and the last MELEE_BOOT_SCENE links on the page -- the #perf render-scale row -- are gone too: they duplicated the Video setting and dropped ?room= on every press, which the #35 ruling makes a real bug rather than a cosmetic one. One correction to this issue's text: it says 'the ports stay as they are' across a save-state load. Per #35 a load now mints a NEW room, so the loader keeps its seat through the reload but re-invites instead of rejoining. Still open on gitea; the owner closes it.

issues.title: Boot flags are bound to the room code, not to the URL
issues.pin: Owner ruling landed: a load mints a new room code. Implemented -- states.mjs withRoom now replaces ?room= instead of preserving it, with a test that fails if the old room rides along. Reason: a preset load is a reload (no snapshot path in the browser build), so the old room already saw this player leave and reassigned the port. Rejoining it would make the two sides disagree about the port map. Unblocks #22.

issues.title: Drop-in join
issues.pin: Taking a free port has to reach a match already running. Blocked, and not on the transport: the browser build defines no MELEE_STATE_SECTIONS, so snapshot_take() refuses every call and netplay is lockstep-only. See #34 and comment 2989 for the prerequisite order.

issues.title: Browser bypasses the lockstep guard
issues.pin: Why drop-in join is blocked: CMakeLists.txt:374 fails the build on a platform with no snapshot sections, and the browser target never reaches that check. Every online session silently degrades to lockstep.

issues.title: Spectators and the port queue
issues.pin: Past four players everybody watches and queues. Server side shipped: a release message frees a port and the first waiter still subscribed gets it, in claim order. The lobby draws the line now: #queue reports how long the queue is and who is next, hidden when nobody waits. It deliberately does not repeat where this user stands -- that is already in the status string, and a second copy of one fact is a second thing to drift. The roster beside it is the other half of this issue: #here lists who is in the room, read off the signalling server's subscriber map, which the close handler already prunes. It is a separate element because membership and queue order are separate facts -- the demo's old "2 watching" count is gone, since no message carried it and the list says more anyway. Measured over three real subscriptions: the server publishes here:[kiri,guest-4f,mango] and the lobby draws "In the room: kiri, guest-4f, mango". The queue is complete for the seat count the game has: with two seats a waiter is a real spectator and the release path promotes them. It no longer waits on a transport for more peers -- that is #40 and out of goal; the invalid #37 it used to cite is closed.

issues.title: TURN relay for symmetric NAT
issues.pin: The fallback this control names. Blocked: this network is cone, so it cannot produce the failing case.

issues.title: Modes become save states
issues.pin: Versus and Training stop being places to go. The port-loss bug is fixed: sessionId keyed on sessionStorage survives the reload, so the loader keeps its seat. Per the #35 ruling a load now opens a NEW room, so the loader re-invites rather than rejoining a room that wrote them off.

issues.title: Verify the port runs on iOS Safari
issues.pin: The disc loads and boots. Measured working on iOS Safari.

issues.title: Flatten the web disc path
issues.pin: What the disc line is waiting on: HTTP Range over a 1.4 GB ISO. The engine reads files by name and fetches blocks on demand, so there is no load percentage; 60% of the disc is FMV that never plays. Gated on measuring the real working set.

issues.title: Disable Start while the disc loads
issues.pin: No disc load exists to wait on: remote-disc.mjs fetches one HTTP Range per block on demand. Start is already gated on a disc being present, at shell.mjs:176.

issues.title: Touch input layer
issues.pin: The shared state object every touch control writes to. One per port.

issues.title: Gamepad API for Bluetooth pads
issues.pin: A real pad claims a port like any other controller. Still open: #30 shipped the per-port connect button and the source picker, but only the GameCube adapter routes input so far, so a plain Bluetooth pad is offered and does not yet play.

issues.title: Mobile CSS: pre-Start controls reachable
issues.pin: A test now fails if this bar moves out of thumb reach on a phone.

issues.title: Settings into tabs
issues.pin: Four tabs of five. Netplay arrived with MELEE_NET_DELAY in #28. Input stays empty because no input setting exists in the engine to put in it -- see #32, measured.

issues.title: 20XX as a select-all
issues.pin: Landed. The parent follows what env_flag_or_20xx reads: an untouched child follows 20XX, a child set by hand keeps its own value, and the URL carries a child only when it disagrees.

issues.title: Port the native launcher settings
issues.pin: Boot-time env route only. Of the 22 demo rows that are not live controls, 10 are built (MELEE_20XX, _BOOT_CSS, _20XX_RULES, UCF, FROZEN_STADIUM, PAUSE, PAUSE_ON_BLUR, SCALE, HITBOXES, NET_DELAY), so 10 of 22. Each is a query param read once in preRun, so changing one costs a page reload. The other 12 are not done: six have no getenv anywhere in src/ and no exported setter, so there is no route to the engine at all (hud_mode, texture filter, custom_textures, free_camera, mute, net_name); the rest are owned by #29 (unlock-all), #32 (four input rows) and #17 (relay). The five audio and aspect controls are not counted here: they went in by a different mechanism, see #42.

issues.title: Training scenarios from a URL
issues.pin: Training is a state loaded into the lobby. Its tools run outside the player ports, so a scenario needs no seat.

issues.title: On-screen control layout
issues.pin: Where the pad layout is chosen. Needs a device in hand: no code decides where a thumb reaches.

issues.title: Accessibility defaults for touch
issues.pin: Tap-jump off, deadzone, curve, C-stick. Defaults chosen; the issue text still argues with itself. Wording only.

issues.title: Mobile layout: full-viewport canvas
issues.pin: The launcher fits this box with no page scroll. (pointer: coarse) and touch-action: none ship, and menu-button.mjs holds the controls. The launcher inside it is now #21's.

issues.title: Optimize the browser build
issues.pin: Measured on the phone: 960x720 holds 60 fps. The 17 fps reading was a cold shader cache, not the render size, so this control is headroom rather than a fix. Lever 2 (dropping EMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS, -1.55 MB) first trapped at frame 2 on a signature mismatch; 14 callback signatures were fixed and at 38cd4e94 the build boots and holds 60 fps for 91 s, though the fixing commit is not named.

issues.title: Browser QoL: resume, pause, settings
issues.pin: Pause-on-blur landed. Resume after refresh and pause on crash did not. Parked.

issues.title: Condense the 20XX children into a closed grid
issues.pin: Measured at 390px: the fold is already closed on load and now holds 2 children, not the 5 this was written against. The issue calls one-per-row the right shape for 2, so the grid would save one 50px row and break the Tournament rules hint, which spans full width. Unlock everything stays out: the owner chose to condense the UI rather than add the C env read. The fold now carries this anchor's id and wraps its children in a .kid-grid, so the board can pin it; the grid is the shape the demo declares at mockup.py:114.

issues.title: Controller connect belongs on the port
issues.pin: Shipped: every tile has this button, and it offers only the sources this browser can do. The page-level WebHID button is gone, and the picker opens from the press. Picking a source labels the port; only the adapter routes input so far, which is #5 and #2.

issues.title: Signify which port is you
issues.pin: Closed. The tile you hold carries a left bar and the word 'you', because colour alone fails a colour-blind reader and a screenshot. The id moves with a claim and a release, and matching is on the server id, so two players with one display name still mark one tile. The spectator line below is the other half, and the queue on it is #23.

issues.title: Fill the Input tab, including controller options
issues.pin: Measured: none of the 4 rows drawn here exists in the engine. No deadzone, stick curve, tap-jump or C-stick mode anywhere in src/pc, in any of the 60 getenv readers, or among the 28 prefs fields in launcher.cpp. The per-port question is moot until something exists to set. The rows are mockup-only; building them needs native input settings first.

issues.title: Load button and save-state modal, instead of a disc chip
issues.pin: The chip read a percentage the browser build cannot measure. The slot becomes a press: Load opens the state menu, which holds the four presets and the states this player saved.

issues.title: Export pc_net_connect so a net session can start (invalid)
issues.pin: INVALID -- the cause was wrong, and closing it rather than rewriting it so the board stops implying a one-line fix. pc_net_connect does not need an export: browser_net_start (platforms/browser/main.c:95) wraps it, is EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE and is already in -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS, and shell.mjs:442 already ccalls it. Two-player netplay runs through that path today, so nothing was blocked. The real limit on a third player is an engine design limit, now tracked as #40: net.c:2161 collapses the player argument to a boolean (net.local = player ? 1 : 0; net.remote = 1 - net.local), there is one remote input ring (net.c:65-68), and per-frame injection fills 2 of the 4 pad ports (net.c:2736,2745).

issues.title: Document the progress board in the architecture map
issues.pin: This board is undocumented in the repo that owns it. docs/ARCHITECTURE-MAP.md (264 lines) and platforms/browser/README.md mention tools/progress/ zero times, so an agent reading the index never learns the board exists, let alone that it is the spec.

issues.title: Gate demo-to-artifact parity; --audit does not cover it
issues.pin: How this panel drifted from the demo without anything failing. --audit compares pins to the tracker and never opens the artifact, so spec->artifact and demo->artifact are ungated. Measured 2026-10-11: the demo declares 27 settings rows across 5 tabs and the build creates 12 across 4, Input absent entirely. An id-attribute grep misses it too -- the demo builds rows from f-strings, so the gate has to walk the TABS row set.

issues.title: Three and four player netplay needs an N-way engine net layer
issues.pin: OUT OF GOAL -- recorded so the board stops blaming a wasm export for it, not because it is queued. The standing goal is two people on two phones, which works. Seating a third is an engine rewrite, measured: the session holds one local and one remote and no player table (net_internal.h:349); net.c:2161 collapses the player argument to a boolean and derives remote = 1 - local, so seats 2 and 3 cannot be named; there is one remote input ring and one have/newest counter (net.c:65-68) that wait_remote waits on (net.c:1569); per-frame injection fills exactly 2 of the 4 pad ports (net.c:2736,2745); the handshake branches on local==0/1 (net_handshake.c:751, net_sync.c:182,251); net_rank.h:18-32 is fixed [2] arrays. There is no PC_NET_MAX_PLAYERS -- PC_LAN_MAX_PEERS 8 (net_lan.h:19) sizes LAN discovery, not seats. Lifting it needs per-seat tables and rings, a wait on the minimum across peers, and a peer-addressed transport. Only then do the browser caps matter, and they are the smaller half: signal.mjs claims are literally [null,null] with a 400 above slot 1 (:6,:65,:99), offer/answer are broadcast with no addressing so 3+ peers cannot pair, shell.mjs holds one RTCPeerConnection, net_rtc.c carries one channel with no peer id, and lobby.mjs:31 PAIRABLE=2 gates the UI.

issues.title: Two players on two real phones through one shared link
issues.pin: The standing goal, and the one pin whose closing needs a measurement no other pin makes. #6 measured two browsers pairing over a routable https origin, one of them phone-shaped -- a viewport, not a phone. This closes when two actual handsets open the same link, both claim a port, and a match runs with the touch overlay driving it on both. Until that is measured the board should not read as done, however green the gates are.

Closed: all five exist in settings.mjs LIVE (volume, music, sfx, reverb, aspect), 5 of 5. Each calls its exported C setter directly while the engine runs (pc_audio_set_volume, _music_volume, _sfx_volume, pc_audio_set_reverb, pc_widescreen_set_mode) and persists in localStorage as melee.live.<fn>. They are never in the URL: a slider behind a page reload would cost the player the match, and a value in the URL would carry your volume to a friend through a shared room link.
